301:     # if voicing is not binary, use linear interpolation
302:     is_binary_voicing = np.all(
303:         np.logical_or(np.equal(voicing, 0), np.equal(voicing, 1))
304:     )
305:     if kind == "nearest" or (kind == "linear" and not is_binary_voicing):
306:         voicing_resampled = scipy.interpolate.interp1d(times, voicing, kind)(times_new)
307:     # otherwise, always use zeroth order
308:     else:
309:         voicing_resampled = scipy.interpolate.interp1d(times, voicing, "zero")(
310:             times_new
311:         )
312: 
313:     return frequencies_resampled, voicing_resampled
314: 
315: 
316: def to_cent_voicing(
317:     ref_time,
318:     ref_freq,
319:     est_time,
320:     est_freq,
321:     est_voicing=None,
322:     ref_reward=None,
323:     base_frequency=10.0,
324:     hop=None,
325:     kind="linear",
326: ):
327:     """Convert reference and estimated time/frequency (Hz) annotations to sampled
328:     frequency (cent)/voicing arrays.
329: 
330:     A zero frequency indicates "unvoiced".
331: 
332:     If est_voicing is not provided, a negative frequency indicates:
333:         "Predicted as unvoiced, but if it's voiced,
334:         this is the frequency estimate".
335: 
336:     If it is provided, negative frequency values are ignored, and the voicing
337:     from est_voicing is directly used.
338: 
339:     Parameters
340:     ----------
341:     ref_time : np.ndarray
342:         Time of each reference frequency value
343: 
344:     ref_freq : np.ndarray
345:         Array of reference frequency values
346: 
347:     est_time : np.ndarray
348:         Time of each estimated frequency value
349: 
350:     est_freq : np.ndarray
351:         Array of estimated frequency values
352: 
353:     est_voicing : np.ndarray
354:         Estimate voicing confidence.
355:         Default None, which means the voicing is inferred from est_freq:
356: 
357:           - frames with frequency <= 0.0 are considered "unvoiced"
358:           - frames with frequency > 0.0 are considered "voiced"
359: 
360:     ref_reward : np.ndarray
361:         Reference voicing reward.
362:         Default None, which means all frames are weighted equally.
363: 
364:     base_frequency : float
365:         Base frequency in Hz for conversion to cents
366:         (Default value = 10.)
367: 
368:     hop : float
369:         Hop size, in seconds, to resample,
370:         default None which means use ref_time
371: 
372:     kind : str
373:         kind parameter to pass to scipy.interpolate.interp1d.
374:         (Default value = 'linear')
375: 
376:     Returns
377:     -------
378:     ref_voicing : np.ndarray
379:         Resampled reference voicing array
380:     ref_cent : np.ndarray
381:         Resampled reference frequency (cent) array
382:     est_voicing : np.ndarray
383:         Resampled estimated voicing array
384:     est_cent : np.ndarray
385:         Resampled estimated frequency (cent) array
386: 
387:     """
388:     # Check if missing sample at time 0 and if so add one
389:     if ref_time[0] > 0:
390:         ref_time = np.insert(ref_time, 0, 0)
391:         ref_freq = np.insert(ref_freq, 0, ref_freq[0])
392:         if ref_reward is not None:
393:             ref_reward = np.insert(ref_reward, 0, ref_reward[0])
394:     if est_time[0] > 0:
395:         est_time = np.insert(est_time, 0, 0)
396:         est_freq = np.insert(est_freq, 0, est_freq[0])
397:         if est_voicing is not None:
398:             est_voicing = np.insert(est_voicing, 0, est_voicing[0])
399: 
400:     # Get separated frequency array and voicing array
401:     ref_freq, ref_voicing = freq_to_voicing(ref_freq, ref_reward)
402:     est_freq, est_voicing = freq_to_voicing(est_freq, est_voicing)
403:     # convert both sequences to cents
404:     ref_cent = hz2cents(ref_freq, base_frequency)
405:     est_cent = hz2cents(est_freq, base_frequency)
406: 
407:     # If we received a hop, use it to resample both
408:     if hop is not None:
409:         # Resample to common time base
410:         ref_cent, ref_voicing = resample_melody_series(
411:             ref_time,
412:             ref_cent,
413:             ref_voicing,
414:             constant_hop_timebase(hop, ref_time.max()),
415:             kind,
416:         )
417:         est_cent, est_voicing = resample_melody_series(
418:             est_time,
419:             est_cent,
420:             est_voicing,
421:             constant_hop_timebase(hop, est_time.max()),
422:             kind,
423:         )
424:     # Otherwise, only resample estimated to the reference time base
425:     else:
426:         est_cent, est_voicing = resample_melody_series(
427:             est_time, est_cent, est_voicing, ref_time, kind
428:         )
429:     # ensure the estimated sequence is the same length as the reference
430:     len_diff = ref_cent.shape[0] - est_cent.shape[0]
431:     if len_diff >= 0:
432:         est_cent = np.append(est_cent, np.zeros(len_diff))
433:         est_voicing = np.append(est_voicing, np.zeros(len_diff))
434:     else:
435:         est_cent = est_cent[: ref_cent.shape[0]]
436:         est_voicing = est_voicing[: ref_voicing.shape[0]]
437: 
438:     return (ref_voicing, ref_cent, est_voicing, est_cent)
439: 
440: 
441: def voicing_recall(ref_voicing, est_voicing):
442:     """Compute the voicing recall given two voicing
443:     indicator sequences, one as reference (truth) and the other as the estimate
444:     (prediction).  The sequences must be of the same length.
445: 
446:     Examples
447:     --------
448:     >>> ref_time, ref_freq = mir_eval.io.load_time_series('ref.txt')
449:     >>> est_time, est_freq = mir_eval.io.load_time_series('est.txt')
450:     >>> (ref_v, ref_c,
451:     ...  est_v, est_c) = mir_eval.melody.to_cent_voicing(ref_time,
452:     ...                                                  ref_freq,
453:     ...                                                  est_time,
454:     ...                                                  est_freq)
455:     >>> recall = mir_eval.melody.voicing_recall(ref_v, est_v)
456:
